rationale: bugs_open/332 is markdown reaching visitors as article text on live sites. The 332 lane routed two findings into this lane's footprint (internal/adapters/websearch/providers/firecrawl.go) and explicitly did not edit the file; this is the producer-side half, and it is committed as 6f0a246de. Both findings verified first-hand against the live DB before acting, not accepted on report. [MEASURED 2026-09-03, 30 days of content_feed_items, 5,863 rows]: 943 rows exactly 200 bytes long (the 332 lane measured 941 — the feed ran between the two reads, which is the expected direction), 288 rows carrying an unclosed '](url' tail, 2 rows carrying U+FFFD. All the damage is source_type='news_search'. Both defects are MANUFACTURED at one line, firecrawl.go's `if len(snippet) > 200 { snippet = snippet[:197] + "..." }`. (1) That is a BYTE slice, so it can split a multi-byte rune — 2 live rows already carry the replacement character. (2) A cut landing inside `[text](url)` leaves a fragment the downstream literal-markdown strip is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to, because its pattern needs the closing paren, so the raw URL reaches visitors as article text. The producer emits syntactically broken markdown and every downstream reader inherits it. The fix makes the cut rune-safe and backs it off a link opening — but only a genuine one ('[' followed by '](' with no ')' after it), so a bare footnote marker like '[1]' is left alone rather than costing real prose. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY IS NOT: the 332 lane offered a contested 'strip markdown BEFORE the cut' transform which would return ~69 chars of real prose per snippet. I declined it and agree with their own read: it writes a lossy transform to disk that the DISABLE_NEWS_MARKDOWN_STRIP kill switch cannot undo, it is on a path shared with web search (prepare_extraction_context and FilterSearchResultsAction read the same column), and cmd/reasoningset/extract.sql rebuilds the triage model's input from that column, so it would make that corpus silently bimodal. Display-time stripping belongs in the shared queryresolve projection they are building — transform at READ, not at WRITE. Dropping a partial link is a different thing and is not lossy in the same sense: it changes the truncation BOUNDARY, removing only bytes that truncation has already made unusable. ALSO DECLINED: making the 200 a config key, which they floated as 'the cheaper instrument for a budget problem is the budget'. Any budget can land mid-link, so it does not fix the class, only its frequency; and web_search has NO ActionInputSpec registered at all (grepped: zero hits), so an optional key there would be added to a surface scripts/audit-optional-key-budget.sh already reports as 'NOT COUNTED — no ActionInputSpec, so the optional surface is UNKNOWABLE, not zero' rather than under the RFC_022 budget. Left as a constant with that reasoning beside it. NOT datahelpers.SafeCut despite it being the estate's rune-safe primitive, and the reason is layering not preference: datahelpers imports database/sql, and nothing under internal/adapters imports datahelpers today — making a small adapter binary depend on platform/orchestration to borrow four lines is the wrong trade, and unicode/utf8 is stdlib and is already the whole of SafeCut's body. Evidence discipline: the link guard was MUTATED to prove it is load-bearing (disabling it reproduces the production shape verbatim — a leaked bare URL with an unclosed '](' — while both 'keeps' tests stay green, so they are not passing because of the trim), and one fixture was found to be 194 bytes, under the 200 budget, truncating NOTHING while passing its own premise; it now asserts it is over budget and that its link closes after the cut before testing anything. verify-head-builds.sh --with --test ./internal/adapters/websearch/... passed against HEAD e50ed792f.

plan.summary: firecrawl.go truncates result snippets with a byte slice at 197 bytes, which splits multi-byte runes (2 live rows carry U+FFFD) and cuts inside markdown links, leaving an unclosed '](url' tail on 288 of 5,863 rows in 30 days. The tail is invisible to the downstream literal-markdown strip because that pattern needs the closing paren, so raw URLs reach visitors as article text (bugs_open/332). This replaces the inline cut with truncateSnippet: rune-safe, and backs the cut off a genuine link opening while leaving bare brackets alone. It deliberately does NOT strip markdown before the cut and does NOT make the budget configurable; both were considered and declined with reasons. Producer-side only — the 332 lane owns the display projection and the historical rows.

edits.rationale: Stop manufacturing a malformed artefact at the producer. Ordering fix candidates by what closes the door: making the producer unable to emit a half-open link makes the bad state unrepresentable going forward, while the 332 lane's downstream pattern remains necessary for the 288 rows already on disk and as the authoritative display seam.

The two failure shapes are production-measured, not invented, and the tests say so. Boundary coverage is a sweep rather than one alignment, because a single lucky boundary proves nothing about rune safety.
edits.sketch: TestTruncateSnippetLeavesShortInputAlone; TestTruncateSnippetNeverSplitsARune (sweeps max=4..300 over 2-byte runes, asserting utf8.ValidString, no U+FFFD, and within budget at every boundary); TestByteSliceTruncationWouldSplitARune (fails if the old byte-slice cut is restored — the mutation guard for the rune half); TestTruncateSnippetDropsAHalfWrittenLink (asserts the fixture is over budget AND that its link closes after the cut BEFORE testing anything, because the first version of this fixture was 194 bytes and exercised nothing); TestTruncateSnippetKeepsACompleteLink; TestTruncateSnippetKeepsABareBracket (the over-trim guard); TestTruncateSnippetOutputIsAlwaysWithinBudget.

grounded_in: firecrawl.go before this change: `if len(snippet) > 200 { snippet = snippet[:197] + "..." }` — a byte slice, no rune handling, no link awareness.
Live census 2026-09-03 over 30 days of content_feed_items: 5,863 rows total; 943 exactly 200 bytes; 288 matching source_summary ~ '\]\([^)]*$'; 2 matching source_summary LIKE '%'||U&'\FFFD'||'%'.
datahelpers.SafeCut at platform/orchestration/datahelpers/data_helpers.go:1020 — the estate's rune-safe primitive; its body is a RuneStart back-off, identical to what this implements locally.

Layering check: `grep -rn 'orchestration/datahelpers' internal/` returns internal/agents/contentcreator, internal/core-manager and internal/tools-api, but NOTHING under internal/adapters; datahelpers imports database/sql.

firecrawl.go is the only provider that truncates: `grep -rn '\[:197\]|> 200' internal/adapters/websearch/providers/*.go` matches this file alone, so this is a single-site fix with no sibling to keep in step.

332 lane's own reasons for leaving strip-before-cut contested: the DISABLE_NEWS_MARKDOWN_STRIP kill switch cannot undo an on-disk transform; prepare_extraction_context and FilterSearchResultsAction share the column; cmd/reasoningset/extract.sql rebuilds the triage model input from it.

web_search has no registered ActionInputSpec (zero hits for RegisterActionInputSpec("web_search"), established by this lane during the 2026-09-02 region-key council round), so the optional-key audit lists it as NOT COUNTED rather than under budget.

Mutation run 2026-09-03: disabling the link guard makes only TestTruncateSnippetDropsAHalfWrittenLink fail, with the leaked bare URL and unclosed '](' visible in the failure output; the two 'keeps' tests stay green under the mutation.
verify-head-builds.sh --with (both files) --test ./internal/adapters/websearch/... ./cmd/web-search-adapter/... : OK against HEAD e50ed792f.
plan.risks: (1) The trim can shorten a snippet by up to one partial link's length, so a summary that previously ended in a broken URL now ends earlier in prose. That is the intent, but it is a visible content change on every future news_search row and a reviewer should agree the boundary choice is not the contested lossy transform. (2) It fixes only rows written AFTER the roll — the 288 already on disk still need the 332 lane's downstream pattern, so neither change alone closes the bug and they must both land. (3) Defence in depth means two places now understand truncated links (this cut and their literal_markdown pattern); they could drift, and the mitigation is that they are independent — the producer stops emitting the shape, the reader stops trusting it. (4) The bare-bracket carve-out is a judgement: a snippet ending '[see' with no '](' keeps a dangling open bracket. It leaks no URL and the strip is not confused by it, so it was left, but a reviewer may prefer trimming that too. (5) Inert until the web-search-adapter image is rebuilt and rolled; the deploy is the owner's call and this lane does not roll it.
